thread:
Ethan Park: Need quick alignment on installer verification error taxonomy before we lock the messages. Support asked for stable error codes so they can triage without screenshot-guessing. Proposal: `RWPV-XXXX` codes (Redwood Private Verify). Thoughts?

Dev Patel: +1 on stable codes. Please no “generic failure” buckets. Support wants: code + 1-line user message + “what to collect” + link to runbook section.

Owen Phillips: From pilot tickets: biggest confusions were (1) hash mismatch after USB transfer, (2) unknown key after rotation, (3) time skew “not yet valid”. If those don’t have distinct codes we’ll be dead.

Jordan Lee: Agree. Also we need a clear split between:
- signature envelope failures (can’t verify)
- manifest integrity failures (manifest doesn’t match bundle)
- policy failures (downgrade blocked, break-glass not allowed)

Marcus Lin: Security req: errors must fail closed by default and be unambiguous (no “maybe safe”). Also avoid leaking key IDs in the *default* console output; OK to put in debug logs.

Kevin Osei: + audit logging: error code should map 1:1 to `bundle_verify.outcome_reason` so SIEM exporters can key off it. If Support invents labels later, we’ll get drift.

Logan Wright: For telemetry/audit, I can emit fields:
- `event_name=bundle_verification`
- `outcome=success|failure|override`
- `reason_code=RWPV-xxxx`
- `bundle_build_id` (if parseable)
- `manifest_digest` (sha256, truncated?)
But I need the canonical list now.

Kira Thompson: Docs request: keep the user-facing messages consistent + add a “Common errors” table. If codes are stable, we can document once and just add rows.

Ethan Park: Cool. Here’s a draft list. Please react / comment.

Ethan Park: **Draft error codes**

Signature / trust
- `RWPV-1001 SIGNATURE_MISSING` — “Signature file not found in bundle.”
- `RWPV-1002 SIGNATURE_INVALID` — “Signature does not match the manifest.”
- `RWPV-1003 KEY_UNTRUSTED` — “Signing key is not trusted by this installer.”
- `RWPV-1004 CERT_NOT_YET_VALID` — “Signature is not yet valid. Check system time.”
- `RWPV-1005 CERT_EXPIRED` — “Signature is expired. Check bundle version/time.”

Manifest / bundle integrity
- `RWPV-2001 MANIFEST_MISSING`
- `RWPV-2002 MANIFEST_PARSE_ERROR`
- `RWPV-2003 MANIFEST_CANONICALIZATION_ERROR` (manifest not in canonical form we sign)
- `RWPV-2004 MANIFEST_HASH_MISMATCH` (manifest sha doesn’t match expected?)
- `RWPV-2005 ARTIFACT_HASH_MISMATCH` (one or more artifacts differ)
- `RWPV-2006 ARTIFACT_MISSING`
- `RWPV-2007 BUNDLE_LAYOUT_INVALID` (wrong paths, extra nesting)

Policy
- `RWPV-3001 DOWNGRADE_BLOCKED`
- `RWPV-3002 BREAK_GLASS_NOT_ALLOWED`
- `RWPV-3003 BREAK_GLASS_USED` (not a failure; install proceeded)

Other
- `RWPV-9001 INTERNAL_ERROR` (only if we truly can’t categorize)

User message format: `ERROR (RWPV-####): <short sentence>.`

Dev Patel: This is close. A few notes:
1) `MANIFEST_HASH_MISMATCH` vs `SIGNATURE_INVALID` — which one do we show when manifest is modified? For Support I’d rather always call it signature invalid unless signature file is missing.
2) Need one explicitly for “bundle is signed but installer doesn’t support signing / too old”. We’ll see that in the field.

Owen Phillips: +1 on (2). Also can we add “hash mismatch likely due to transfer/unzip tooling” as a hint in `ARTIFACT_HASH_MISMATCH`? That’s what SUP-31892 was.

Jordan Lee: Re (1):
- If manifest content changed => signature verification fails => `SIGNATURE_INVALID`
- `MANIFEST_HASH_MISMATCH` might be redundant unless we have a *separate* expected digest (like manifest listed in a header) which we don’t.
We do have `manifest.digest` we compute and log; no need for a code.

Marcus Lin: Agree: don’t overfit. Keep codes tied to security semantics:
- signature missing
- signature invalid
- untrusted key
- validity window (time)
- content mismatch (artifact)

Kevin Osei: For SIEM, fewer reasons is better *as long as* Support can triage. Artifact mismatch must carry artifact path(s) in logs, but code can be one.

Logan Wright: I can include `details.artifacts_failed` in local audit log file (not exported by default). For exported event, probably just `failed_artifact_count`.

Ethan Park: Ok, removing `MANIFEST_HASH_MISMATCH`. Also adding an “installer too old” code.

Kira Thompson: Please keep the names consistent (all caps, underscores). Also: `CERT_*` names might confuse non-PKI folks; maybe `SIGNATURE_*` + `TIME_*`?

Dev Patel: +1. Support will read “cert” and assume TLS.

Ethan Park: Updated naming:
- `RWPV-1004 TIME_NOT_YET_VALID`
- `RWPV-1005 TIME_EXPIRED`

Marcus Lin: Works.

Jordan Lee: For `MANIFEST_CANONICALIZATION_ERROR`: should only happen if someone hand-edited manifest or used old bundler. That’s useful for Support. Keep it.

Owen Phillips: Also: add `RWPV-2008 MANIFEST_SCHEMA_VERSION_UNSUPPORTED` maybe? We’ll hit forward-compat issues.

Ethan Park: Good call. Add `RWPV-2008 MANIFEST_SCHEMA_UNSUPPORTED`.

Kevin Osei: If you add that, please ensure the audit event includes `manifest_schema_version` (if parseable) even on failure.

Logan Wright: Yup.

Allison Grant: Jumping in: please standardize severity mapping for logs:
- `RWPV-1xxx` => ERROR
- `RWPV-2xxx` => ERROR
- `RWPV-3xxx` => ERROR except `BREAK_GLASS_USED` => WARN
- `RWPV-9xxx` => ERROR
And make sure we don’t log raw bundle paths if they may contain customer usernames; ok to log basename.

Ethan Park: Noted.

Dev Patel: We also need the “what to collect” guidance to be consistent. Suggest every failure prints:
- bundle path
- manifest digest
- installer version
- command to run `installer bundle inspect --verify --output report.json`
Then Support asks for report.json + logs.

Kira Thompson: Please keep the printed guidance short and point to docs. Maybe:
“Run: `redwood-private-installer bundle inspect <path> --verify --report verify-report.json` and attach verify-report.json to your support case.”

Ethan Park: Perfect.

Ethan Park: **Final-ish list v1**
Signature / trust
- `RWPV-1001 SIGNATURE_MISSING`
- `RWPV-1002 SIGNATURE_INVALID`
- `RWPV-1003 KEY_UNTRUSTED`
- `RWPV-1004 TIME_NOT_YET_VALID`
- `RWPV-1005 TIME_EXPIRED`
- `RWPV-1006 INSTALLER_SIGNING_UNSUPPORTED` (installer too old / feature flag off)

Manifest / bundle integrity
- `RWPV-2001 MANIFEST_MISSING`
- `RWPV-2002 MANIFEST_PARSE_ERROR`
- `RWPV-2003 MANIFEST_CANONICALIZATION_ERROR`
- `RWPV-2004 MANIFEST_SCHEMA_UNSUPPORTED`
- `RWPV-2005 ARTIFACT_HASH_MISMATCH`
- `RWPV-2006 ARTIFACT_MISSING`
- `RWPV-2007 BUNDLE_LAYOUT_INVALID`

Policy
- `RWPV-3001 DOWNGRADE_BLOCKED`
- `RWPV-3002 BREAK_GLASS_NOT_ALLOWED`
- `RWPV-3003 BREAK_GLASS_USED` (WARN + audit marker)

Other
- `RWPV-9001 INTERNAL_ERROR`

If no objections by EOD I’ll drop into installer + send to Docs/Support.

Owen Phillips: Looks good. For `ARTIFACT_HASH_MISMATCH` message, can we add hint: “This can happen if the bundle was modified during transfer/extraction. Re-transfer and re-extract using the documented method.”

Marcus Lin: Ok as long as it doesn’t imply “maybe safe to ignore”. Make it a remediation, not a downgrade.

Ethan Park: Yup: “Install blocked. Re-transfer…”.

Kevin Osei: Please ensure `BREAK_GLASS_USED` includes `override_ticket_id` (operator-provided) in the audit record. We need traceability.

Logan Wright: I’ll make it a required flag when override is invoked: `--break-glass-ticket <id>`.

Dev Patel: :thumbsup: This will help a lot. I’ll update the Support macro templates once merged.

Kira Thompson: Send me the final table once you merge; I’ll align the docs error reference.

Ethan Park: Will do. Thanks all.
